episodes.179380: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a warm and unstable airmass.
episodes.179452: A stagnant pattern combined with unusually moist air, led to widespread heavy rain that|generated a round of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.179496: Upslope flow and weak surface convergence along a dryline near the Texas/New Mexico state line allowed for scattered thunderstorms to develop late in the afternoon into the evening on the third. Weak mid level winds and a moist atmosphere created a favorable environment for efficient rainfall producing storms. While the storms did produce some large hail and damaging wind gusts, the primary threat from the storms was the intense rainfall rates. Slow moving storms combined with the intense rates to create flash flooding in and around Friona (Parmer County) and Tulia (Swisher County).
episodes.179510: Showers and strong to severe thunderstorms sprouted in the afternoon and evening of June 3rd as a backdoor cold front approached and then pushed across the area. One inch hail fell in the towns of Pennsboro and Middlebourne, and damaging wind gusts resulted in multiple downed trees in the Pennsboro, French Creek, and Rock Cave areas. A tree struck by lightning in Salem fell on power lines. Later in the evening, another tree was struck in Parkersburg and split in two. One intersection in Beckley also flooded due to heavy rain.
episodes.179519: Scattered thunderstorms associated with an upper-level low produced localized marginally severe hail and wind gusts over portions of western Maryland and eastern West Virginia.
episodes.179543: A weak upper level disturbance passed over northern NM helping to invigorate another round of afternoon thunderstorms along and east of the central mountain chain of NM. This isolated to scattered activity covered an area stretching from the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains across much of eastern NM. Heavy rains over and near the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar caused flash flooding in the Coyote Creek State Park. Strong to severe storms also produced large hail ranging from Mora County to Roosevelt County.
episodes.179613: Showers and strong thunderstorms sprouted in the afternoon and evening of June 3rd as a backdoor cold front approached and then pushed across the area. In the town of Haysi, strong wind gusts from passing storms resulted in a downed tree.
episodes.179653: Daytime instability combined with lake breezes and outflow boundaries to create isolated thunderstorms during the afternoon on Saturday (6/3).  The strongest storm produced hail up to one inch.
episodes.179676: A cold front dropped southwestward from New England into Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of June 3, 2023, spawning scattered thunderstorms. SBCAPE was moderately high (>2000 J/kg), and deep layer (0-6 km) shear of 40 kts was supportive of supercells across the eastern half of Pennsylvania. Perhaps the most notable aspects of this event were the large hail and the northeast-southwest cell movement.
episodes.179709: One storm in Northeastern Pennsylvania took advantage of limited instability in the region and quickly became severe with large hail. No damage, other than power outages, was mentioned in the lone report.
episodes.179833: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures and precipitation produced high and fast flow on drainages in several west-central counties.
episodes.179847: Thunderstorms began to develop during the afternoon of June 3rd across parts of East and Northeast Texas, extending eastward into portions of Northwest Louisiana. Strong daytime heating and dew points in the middle 60s to lower 70s allowed for modest air mass destabilization, with as much as 1500-2000 J/kg of instability from East Texas into much of neighboring Northwest Louisiana. Deep layer flow was weak, resulting in slow moving storms and very little shear in the background environment. Given this regime, storms generally posed a brief severe risk and remained very pulse in nature, with an increasing threat of flash flooding throughout the afternoon. Numerous local storm reports were documented of large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding. Unfortunately, one flash flood related fatality was reported when a male driver tried to drive through floodwaters on Hearne Avenue in Shreveport. The truck he was driving in quickly took on water, and while his passenger was able to escape, the driver drowned in the high water.
episodes.179848: Thunderstorms began to develop during the afternoon of June 3rd across parts of East and Northeast Texas, extending eastward into portions of Northwest Louisiana. Strong daytime heating and dew points in the middle 60s to lower 70s allowed for modest air mass destabilization, with as much as 1500-2000 J/kg of instability from East Texas into much of neighboring Northwest Louisiana. Deep layer flow was weak, resulting in slow moving storms and very little shear in the background environment. Given this regime, storms remained pulse in nature and generally posed a large hail and damaging wind threat throughout the afternoon. Numerous local storm reports were documented with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180402: Pulse thunderstorms paired with surface boundary interaction resulted in damaging thunderstorm wind and a couple large hail reports.
episodes.180765: A pre-frontal trough along the western North Carolina Piedmont led to the development of isolated to scattered showers and storms across the northwest Piedmont of central North Carolina. A few storms became severe, producing numerous trees down across Forsyth, Guilford, and Davidson Counties.
episodes.181315: A weak upper trough moved out across of the southern High Plains during the afternoon of the 2nd, leading to widespread convection across the region. A storm across Jefferson County became briefly organized, producing a severe-criteria wind gust.
episodes.181316: A cluster of thunderstorms became briefly organized across east-central into southeast Oklahoma during the early afternoon of the 3rd. A few reports of damaging wind gusts, large hail and flooding were received in around the community of Ada.
episodes.181335: The combination of westerly flow aloft, moderate to strong instability and a dryline resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across portions of west central Texas. A few the storms were supercell thunderstorms, which merged into a line of thunderstorms while moving east across the area. The severe storms produced large hail and isolated damaging winds.
episodes.181466: A supercell thunderstorm formed along a dryline near the Big Bend and moved into South Central Texas. This storm produced large hail. This storm later morphed into a squall line that produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.181469: Thunderstorms developed along a surface trough in Central Texas and moved across the northern portion of South Central Texas. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.181512: June began with river flooding along Clear Creek near Chinook, which reached Major Flood Stage for the second time this spring. In fact, Clear Creek recorded its third highest crest on record, as of writing. Fergus County, especially locations south of Lewistown, also experienced flooding due to heavy rainfall. Elsewhere, isolated severe thunderstorms occurred as a spring-like storm system moved across the area.
episodes.181519: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms the 2nd through the 4th brought high winds, flooding, and some landspout tornadoes to the combined Panhandles. June 2nd brought high winds and flooding to both the Oklahoma and Texas Panhandle. The moisture continued into the 3rd and 4th but with slower moving storms and residual outflow boundaries from the 2nd storms produced heavy long lasting rainfall, as well as landspout tornadoes to the TX Panhandle. One landspout did touch down in Amarillo causing some damage. One of the boundaries that helped produce that landspout also caused storms to linger around Amarillo causing some historic flooding with the city having to pump water out of local playa and storm collection lakes well into July.
episodes.181712: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening hours of the 3rd, as a weak upper level disturbance translated into the area. Moderately strong instability combined with weak wind shear to support some severe thunderstorms, with damaging wind gusts and hail up to nickel size.
episodes.181713: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon and evening hours of the 3rd, as a weak upper level disturbance translated into the area. Moderately strong instability combined with weak wind shear to support some severe thunderstorms that produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.181739: A couple of storms became severe and produced one inch diameter hail.
episodes.181837: Showers and thunderstorms developed over the Poconos and Lehigh Valley, with a few severe storms mixed in.
episodes.181918: A cold front pushed south across northwest North Carolina, sparking severe thunderstorms in the region. Winds from the severe thunderstorms brought down umerous trees and power lines, creating power outages that affected several thousand homes in the Eden area.
episodes.181919: A cold front pushed south through Southside Virginia, sparking one severe thunderstorm to produce damaging winds in Henry County.
episodes.182023: Diurnally driven thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of June 3rd, 2023.  The afternoon and early thunderstorms produced isolated wind gusts to 60 mph.
episodes.182093: Thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front the afternoon of June 3rd. With mid-level dry air prompting high DCAPE values (over 1000J/kg), damaging wind gusts were the main concern. However, hail the size of quarters fell in a few isolated storms due to higher terrain prompting a lower freezing level and a few storms mergers.
episodes.182094: Thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front the afternoon of June 3rd. With mid-level dry air prompting high DCAPE values (over 1000J/kg), damaging wind gusts were the main concern. However, hail the size of quarters fell in a few isolated storms due to higher terrain prompting a lower freezing level and a few storms mergers.
episodes.182149: A large closed low had developed over the northern Great Plains with a weaker shortwave trough to its south. These features helped to initiate afternoon thunderstorms off the higher elevations of west Texas and southeast New Mexico. These strong to severe thunderstorms produced isolated areas of large hail and severe winds as they moved east.
episodes.182153: A large closed upper-low was located over the northern Great Plains with a shortwave trough to the south within the sub-tropical jet stream. These features helped bring rich moisture and instability into the region. Widespread strong to severe thunderstorms developed across much of the region. The Permian Basin and the Stockton Plateau were the two main areas of note. Severe winds, large hail. and a brief tornado was observed in this northern complex. To the south, several long-track, cyclic supercells produced tornadoes and very large hail over rural portions of Pecos and Terrell Counties.
episodes.182158: An unusual pattern set up was in place on Saturday June 3, 2022. A cold front was dropping southwest into the state from the northeast, resulting in strong storms along the boundary in the far eastern portion of the state and moving westward instead of the usual eastward direction. The unstable air led to shower and storm development, with some of the strongest storms setting up across Pike County. Overall these storms led to multiple reports of tree damage across the county. Martin County also received a tree down due to an outflow boundary from the larger storm.
episodes.182292: Scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the evening. A couple of the storms produced brief severe weather in the Piedmont.
episodes.182360: Lightning struck a naphtha storage tank at Calcasieu Refining.
episodes.182388: A stagnant pattern with weak easterly flow led to a diurnal development of thunderstorms, with one water-loaded storm collapsing with a burst of locally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.182392: A fairly typical summertime regime was in place with abundant Gulf moisture throughout the atmosphere. As the day progressed, sea breeze boundaries became the focal point for thunderstorm initiation and ample instability enhanced intensity of a few storms. One storm in Assumption Parish was able to strengthen enough to produce severe hail.
episodes.182590: A very moist, easterly surface flow was in place across the Billings area. An area of moderate to heavy rain, with an occasional embedded thunderstorm, positioned itself over western Yellowstone County during the evening hours of the 2nd. Many areas were flooded, especially the west side of Billings.
episodes.182784: During the afternoon and evening hours of June 2nd, storms produced severe winds over portions of Missouri.
episodes.182840: A deep flow of tropical moisture continued over South Florida associated with Tropical Storm Arlene over the NE Gulf of Mexico. This along with instability aided by a jet stream aloft led to the formation of strong and severe thunderstorms across SE Florida.
episodes.182843: A deep flow of tropical moisture continued over South Florida associated with Tropical Storm Arlene over the NE Gulf of Mexico. This along with instability aided by a jet stream aloft led to the formation of strong and severe thunderstorms across SE Florida.

episodes.183097: A severe thunderstorm produced wind damage in portions of Chicot County.
episodes.193592: Thunderstorms brought hail to portions of northern Utah.
